title: What is Index Rebalancing and Why Does it Matter to Your Investments?
description: Index rebalancing is like updating a shopping basket (stock market index) to ensure it accurately reflects the market. It happens regularly, typically every s.

faq.a: Free-float market capitalisation is the portion of a company's total market value that is readily available for trading by the general public, excluding shares held by promoters, government, or other locked-in entities.

faq.q: How often does index rebalancing happen?
faq.a: Major indices like the Nifty 50 and Sensex typically undergo rebalancing twice a year, usually semi-annually.

faq.q: Do all companies in an index have the same weight?
faq.a: No, companies in an index usually have different weights, which are typically determined by their free-float market capitalisation. Larger free-float market cap companies have a higher weight.

faq.q: Can a company be removed from an index even if it's profitable?
faq.a: Yes, profitability is not the sole criterion. A company can be removed if it no longer meets other eligibility criteria, such as sufficient free-float market capitalisation, liquidity, or if it's replaced by a larger, more eligible company.

faq.q: Does rebalancing affect my direct stock investments?
faq.a: If you directly own shares of a company being added or removed, there might be short-term price movements due to institutional buying or selling. However, for long-term investors, the fundamental health of the company usually matters more than short-term index-related movements.
